newsitem.title: UK: UK government hostile to EMU on balance - Rifkind.
newsitem.headline: UK government hostile to EMU on balance - Rifkind.

text.p: British foreign secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Wednesday that, on balance, the government was hostile to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"On balance we are hostile to a single currency, but we accept you have to think very carefully about these matters before you rule them out completely," he told BBC Radio in an interview.
Rifkind said the government has no commitment in principle to joining EMU.

"That is why (Prime Minister) John Major negotiated the opt out. But we will come to a final decision on whether Britain should cooperate when the decisions are taken as to whether there should be a single currency and who should join, and that is round about the end of this year," he said.
Rifkind will meet with leading German politicians in Bonn later and make the second in a series of speeches setting out Britain's vision of a flexible Europe of freely cooperating nation states.
